notes: §1985:XI.4.1.2 prints MERGE file-name-1 {ON {ASCENDING | DESCENDING} KEY {data-name-1} ...} ... [COLLATING SEQUENCE IS alphabet-name-1] USING file-name-2 {file-name-3} ... {OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS procedure-name-1 [{THROUGH | THRU} procedure-name-2] | GIVING {file-name-4} ...}. The grammar's mergeStatement fixes that order, SortBinder.BindMerge requires two USING files and one of OUTPUT PROCEDURE or GIVING (COBOL1757) and an SD file-name-1, and VersionConformancePass.VisitSortCollatingPhrase refuses the 2002 alphabet-name-2 and FOR ALPHANUMERIC / FOR NATIONAL forms at 85 (COBOL0872), so only alphabet-name-1 reaches SortBindCollating. Probed at 85 (classes b, c, e): two USING files with OUTPUT PROCEDURE, with OUTPUT PROCEDURE OUTP THRU OUTP, with GIVING OUT1 OUT2, with COLLATING SEQUENCE IS A1, with two key phrases and with a key list merge and run; one USING file (the witness) and no OUTPUT/GIVING COBOL1757, no USING, no key phrase, KEY with no data-name, WITH DUPLICATES, INPUT PROCEDURE and COLLATING written twice COBOL5506, OUTPUT PROCEDURE with GIVING and COLLATING after USING COBOL2269, IS A1 A2 and both FOR forms COBOL0872, an FD file-name-1 and an SD in USING COBOL1757.

next.reason: 1985: "[ COLLATING SEQUENCE IS alphabet-name-1 ]"; 2023: "COLLATING SEQUENCE IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ] / FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 / FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2". The MERGE format is otherwise the same, but 2023's COLLATING SEQUENCE phrase adds alphabet-name-2 and the FOR ALPHANUMERIC/FOR NATIONAL forms. 2023 therefore accepts programs that 1985 refuses.
